records.selection_criteria: Exploratory manual search for customs, cargo release, or manifest-processing delays reported during the study period in the six study countries, plus targeted searches for named suppliers. Include reviewed official bulletins or attributed reports when their actual scope is clear. Publication in the study period alone does not establish that an event began or ended within it.

sources_searched.outcome: Included an attributed report of Malaysia vessel documentation delays.
Reviewed the same Malaysian industry executive's account; not independent corroboration.
Included reporting of Philippine manifest-submission delays attributed to E2M limitations.
Direct retrieval of the official Philippine memorandum returned HTTP 403; not independently reviewed.
Included attributed Philippine airport cargo clearance statistics and concerns.
Reviewed related airport congestion reporting; its discussion of the same clearance percentages does not independently establish the statistics.
Included third-party reproduction of CBP bulletin 64877951.
Official source for bulletin 64877951; fetch returned a page without the bulletin body.
Included third-party reproduction of CBP bulletin 64970723.
Reviewed another reproduction of bulletin 64970723; it is not an independent account.
Included third-party reproduction of CBP bulletin 65533265.
Possible China lead; direct retrieval returned HTTP 403, so no record was included.
Search found Singapore contingency guidance, but it does not by itself establish an actual customs-delay incident.

known_coverage_gaps: Exploratory working database; searches were not exhaustive across companies, sources, languages, or countries.
No reviewed, supplier-specific customs-delay report or graph entity match was identified in the targeted searches; this is not evidence that none exists.
No qualifying Singapore, Taiwan, or China incident was independently reviewed and included. A China lead and the official Philippine memorandum were inaccessible.
Actual incident start and end dates are unknown for the included records; publication dates are not a substitute for event dates.
The CBP bulletins concern processing or notification issues and do not establish case-study shipment delays. The April and May notification issues may be related.
The included industry claims and reproduced bulletins still need primary-source review or independent corroboration where applicable.
None of these records establishes an empirical delay distribution, probability, supplier impact, or temporal overlap with a specific shipment.
records.licence_notes: Source permissions and redistribution terms have not been verified. Store only concise attributed factual summaries and source links; do not redistribute full reports.
records.review_method: Manually read each included source or identified reproduction, preserve its attribution and precise reported scope, distinguish publication dates from incident dates and observed durations from thresholds or expectations, and leave supplier matches unassigned. File hashes describe the working files as of this review and must be refreshed when those files change. Search windows are separately labelled candidate-retrieval aids, not inferred incident intervals.

records.selection_criteria: Exploratory manual collection of specific carrier or cargo-vessel incidents reported in or relevant to the study jurisdictions during the study period. The Strait of Malacca fire is included because a later report identifies Port Klang as the intended inspection location; incident jurisdiction is unverified. Supplier names were searched, but contextual incidents are not treated as supplier matches.

sources_searched.outcome: Included an official report on WAN HAI A17's collision off Guangzhou.
Included reporting of the Kyparissia fire and Maersk's statement.
Included preliminary official investigation information on the ONE HENRY HUDSON fire.
Reviewed first-responder reporting on the same ONE HENRY HUDSON fire.
Included attributed reporting on the Zeal Lumos collision in Taiwan.
Included reporting attributed to the Philippine Coast Guard concerning Span Asia 39.
Included attributed reporting of the CMA CGM PETRA fire and its intended inspection at Port Klang.
Direct retrieval of the carrier advisory returned HTTP 403; not independently reviewed.
Reviewed official investigation of general cargo ship Xin Feng; excluded from this initial set because a connection to the selected study shipments was not established.
Identified a Singapore-registered vessel incident off India; excluded because registration alone does not establish an incident in a study country.
Official Taiwan investigation confirms the Zeal Lumos collision date as 1 April 2026.
Reviewed the original secondary report identifying Kaohsiung and describing the collision and port response.

known_coverage_gaps: Exploratory research is not exhaustive across suppliers, vessels, languages, dates, carriers, or jurisdictions.
No incident was verified as affecting a selected supplier, shipment, or graph entity; an empty match list is not proof of no impact.
No Singapore-located incident is included; vessel registration alone does not establish incident location.
Most reports do not establish an end date, actual shipment delay, or vessel identity match to graph records.
The Taiwan collision date was checked against an official source; operational details and the Malaysia secondary report still need original-source review. The PETRA carrier advisory was inaccessible.
Vessel charterer, owner, operator, flag, and contractual carrier are distinct; reported names must not be equated without review.
Records are not calibrated event probabilities and may overlap with future port disruption, cargo loss, or natural hazard evidence.
records.licence_notes: Source permissions and redistribution terms have not been verified. Store only concise attributed factual summaries and source links; do not redistribute full reports.
records.review_method: Manually read the linked reports; distinguish incident location from vessel flag, stated incident dates from publication dates, and fire or response duration from shipment delay. Attribute secondary claims and leave entity matches unassigned. File hashes describe working files at this review and must be refreshed when those files change. records.selection_criteria: Initial comparison of USD against the five non-US study currencies using two published observations within the study period. Federal Reserve pairs use 2 January 2025 and 30 September 2026; the Philippine peso comparison uses 31 January 2025 and 30 September 2026.

sources_searched.outcome: Reviewed 2 January 2025 H.10 observations for CNY, MYR, SGD and TWD.
Reviewed 30 September 2026 H.10 observations for the same four currencies.
Reviewed H.10 rate definition and caveat that archived releases may not reflect subsequent revisions.
Reviewed Philippine peso per US dollar end-of-period rates for January 2025 and September 2026.
Reviewed the 31 January 2025 Philippine reference bulletin for the start rate.
Reviewed the 30 September 2026 Philippine daily rate.

known_coverage_gaps: Two endpoint rates per pair do not provide daily paths, volatility, a probability distribution, or the largest intra-period moves.
The peso comparison has a later start date and a different source and rate convention than the Federal Reserve pairs.
The percentage change is calculated from the displayed rates; it is not directly reported by either central bank.
Archived H.10 releases are not revised; the Philippine web tables may change, and source conditions remain unverified.
USD is a reference comparison only; shipment invoicing, supplier exposure, hedging, conversion costs and actual losses have not been verified.
No reviewed entity or shipment matches are established.
records.licence_notes: Source permissions and redistribution terms have not been independently verified. Store concise numerical observations and source links, not complete source files.
records.review_method: Manually compare the published country-labelled source tables and Philippine bulletin, record dates and quote direction, and calculate the percent change as (ending rate / starting rate - 1) * 100 rounded to two decimals. The source field points to the end observation; start sources are documented in the records and manifest. File hashes describe working files at this review and must be refreshed when those files change. Search windows are separately labelled candidate-retrieval aids, not inferred incident intervals.

records.selection_criteria: Exploratory public-source search for specific cyber incidents or explicitly labelled claims concerning the case-study company names during the study period. An unverified claim is recorded as a claim, not a confirmed incident; general advisories and events outside the period are excluded.

sources_searched.outcome: Reviewed and recorded an explicitly alleged ransomware-group listing naming Flex Ltd. The publisher warns that such claims may not be independently verified.
Reviewed legal investigation discussing the same unconfirmed attacker claim; not independent confirmation.
Reviewed a second report of the same attacker claim, not independent confirmation of a breach.
Reviewed a separate listing that explicitly states the threat-actor claim was not verified. Other exposure counts on the page are not necessarily related and were not recorded.
Identified general ransomware information; excluded because it does not establish a case-study supplier incident.
Identified general ransomware advisory in search results; not used as evidence of a case-study supplier incident.

known_coverage_gaps: Searches were exploratory, not exhaustive across names, aliases, languages, regulators, and public disclosures.
The single recorded Flex listing is an unverified attacker allegation, not a confirmed incident; multiple reports may share the same underlying claim.
No selected supplier, facility, incident date, affected service, shipment, or operational impact was verified or matched to Neo4j.
No other confirmed case-study supplier cyberattack was identified in the targeted searches; this is not evidence that none occurred.
The record does not support a probability estimate or establish the scope of any hypothetical compromise.
records.licence_notes: Source permissions and redistribution terms have not been independently verified. Store concise references and attributed claims, not full source text or sensitive data.
records.review_method: Manually read accessible vendor and legal reports, record the source's explicit alleged status, retain unknown incident fields as null, and do not infer identity matches or operational effects. The record documents a claim rather than a verified attack. File hashes describe working files at this review and must be refreshed when those files change. Search windows are separately labelled candidate-retrieval aids, not inferred incident intervals.

records.selection_criteria: Exploratory manual collection of specific increases in fuel, electricity and container freight rates during the study period in or between study countries. Include source-reported market and customer scope; residential benchmarks and route indices are contextual evidence, not supplier costs.

sources_searched.outcome: Included official Peninsular Malaysia diesel price increase for July 2025.
Included Bernama reporting of the finance ministry's March 2026 diesel increase and noted land-logistics subsidy conditions.
Reviewed previous week's March 2026 retail diesel price.
Included the utility's June-to-July 2025 typical residential rate increase, not an industrial rate.
Included Singapore's reported Q3 2026 regulated household electricity tariff and prior-quarter difference.
Official regulator page returned an automated-access challenge; not directly reviewed.
Included the reported Drewry Shanghai-to-Los Angeles spot freight assessment and rounded weekly change.
Reviewed the previous week's Drewry route assessment.
Reviewed the 3 to 9 July 2025 baseline diesel price and effective period.

known_coverage_gaps: Exploratory research is not exhaustive across dates, fuels, energy customers, routes, countries, and languages.
No supplier invoice, electricity contract, fuel eligibility, freight booking, consumption, or actual increased expense was verified.
Electricity benchmarks are residential; they must not be used as industrial rates without independent evidence.
The freight observation is a China-to-US spot index and does not establish an observed shipment route or actual rate paid.
Malaysia's subsidised diesel schemes and regional price differences mean the retail rate cannot be assumed for land logistics.
Dates indicate published effective periods or assessment dates; exact monthly billing dates and source publication dates remain unknown where null.
Overlap with currency, tariff, geopolitical, or carrier evidence requires review to avoid double counting.
records.licence_notes: Source permissions and index redistribution terms have not been independently verified. Store concise attributed factual observations and links, not full source text or copyrighted index datasets.
records.review_method: Manually read the accessible source pages, retain currency, unit, dates and market/customer scope, and calculate percentage change from baseline and observed rates where the source does not report it. Keep the Drewry-reported rounded 57 percent distinct from the approximately 57.20 percent calculated from displayed prices. File hashes describe working files at this review and must be refreshed when those files change. Search windows are separately labelled candidate-retrieval aids, not inferred incident intervals.
